title: Relativity bar colors a neutral 1.0 value as danger (red), inconsistent with heatmap semantics
description: The relativity bar uses background: val >= 1 ? danger-rgb : chart-below-rgb. A value of exactly 1.0 (a neutral relativity, i.e. no effect) is rendered with the 'danger' (above-1) color. The rest of the rating UI's heatmap (ratingTableUtils.relativityColor/relativityTextColor) treats values within ±0.005 of 1.0 as neutral/transparent and only colors dev > 0.005 as danger. So a neutral factor level is shown red here, conflicting with the established convention and over-emphasizing no-op relativities.
evidence: OneWayEditor.tsx:155 background: val >= 1 ? 'rgba(var(--danger-rgb), .35)' : 'rgba(var(--chart-below-rgb), .35)'. Contrast ratingTableUtils.ts:84-86 relativityColor where dev>0.005 => danger, dev<-0.005 => below, else transparent. val===1 falls into '>=1' => danger.
